correctness.rationale: The cyclic prime translation S acts as one J_p(1) over state characteristic p; Z=S−I has Z^p=0 and exactly one nilpotent chain. For subgroup H of order d even, power sums sum_{h∈H}h^j vanish for 1≤j<d and equal d at j=d, so A−dI=(S−I)^d U(S−I) with U(0)=d/d!≠0. The kernel dimensions min(dt,p) imply blocks (k+1,k,...,k) with k=(p−1)/d; the exact eigenvalue d is nonzero, hence invertibility. For ℓ=ord_p(d)>1, A^p=dI; A^t−I has zero kernel except when ℓ|t; if ℓ|t and p∤t it has the same kernel as A−dI of dimension d, and for pℓ|t it is zero. Subtracting nested fixed populations yields orbit lengths 1,ℓ,pℓ and counts 1,(Q^d−1)/ℓ,(Q^p−Q^d)/(pℓ). Independently constructed finite matrices at (p,k,d)=(7,3,2),(13,3,4),(19,3,6) and confirmed nilpotent ranks [2,4,6,7], [4,8,12,13], [6,12,18,19] for increasing powers, compatible with the block claims. Quantifiers require odd p, even d and Q=p^f, not arbitrary state characteristic.

value.rationale: An exact, uniform Jordan decomposition and all-cycle census for the natural prime-order generalized Paley neighbor-sum system is a meaningful finite-field dynamics classification. It identifies only three possible least periods independently of size and gives their exact populations and zeta function, a substantive structural refinement of adjacency spectra.

limitations: Works only in defining characteristic and for prime vertex count; no general q-vertex graph or other characteristic claims.
The first-nonzero binomial coefficient is an elementary representation-theoretic step, raising potential broader theorem priority risk.
